newsitem.title: Italy: SOCCER-INTER MILAN, VICENZA AND JUVENTUS WIN IN CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTER MILAN, VICENZA AND JUVENTUS WIN IN CUP.

text.p: Inter Milan, Vicenza and Juventus all reached the last eight of the Italian Cup on Wednesday but European champions Juventus needed luck against part-timers Nocerina to get there.

Inter defeated Cagliari 2-1 at the San Siro stadium, setting up a quarter-final clash with Juventus who needed an own goal to clinch a hard-fought 2-1 win against third division giant-slayers Nocerina.
Vicenza beat second division Genoa 1-0 with a 61st-minute goal by Giovanni Cornacchini.
All three matches were replays of drawn third-round ties.
Serie A leaders Inter took the lead against Cagliari in the 35th minute through defender Massimo Paganin, whose 25-metre blast left goalkeeper Beniamino Abate helpless.
Englishman Roy Hodgson's club then laid siege to Cagliari's goal.

French international midfielder Youri Djorkaeff, striker Maurizio Ganz and former Italy midfielder Nicola Berti all came close before Chile's Ivan Zamorano scored with a brilliant bicycle kick two minutes from time.
Cagliari's goal came from an own goal by French international defender Jocelyn Angloma in the 85th minute.

Juventus's win at Turin's Delle Alpi stadium was more of a cliffhanger, with serie C's bottom side Nocerina threatening to eliminate the European champions after already knocking out serie A clubs Piacenza and Perugia.

Another upset looked possible when Nocerina, who earned the lucrative replay by drawing with Juventus 0-0 last month, took the lead in the 39th minute through a brilliantly lobbed goal by Franco Marchegiani.
But Juventus, whose absentees included in-form Croatian striker Alen Boksic, bounced back just before halftime with a headed equaliser by tough Uruguayan defender Paolo Montero.

A lucky bounce two minutes after the break turned out to be enough to clinch the tie for Juventus. A shot by midfielder Alessandro Del Piero bounced off Nocerina defender Giovanni Di Rocco and into the net.
Nocerina, who changed their coach last month, come from Nocera Inferiore, a run-down town in the Naples hinterland. Juventus are third in serie A, two points behind Inter.
